stem: (Select TWO.) Aurora Fittings wants two independent proofs that a new provisioning approach is genuine declarative Infrastructure as Code before they adopt it for every project. Which two observations provide that evidence?

choices.text: Follow a documented runbook of console steps that provisions the same infrastructure by hand, in the same order, for every new environment.
The configuration file is committed to version control and used every time the infrastructure is created or changed.
The file states which resources should exist once finished, without listing the ordered steps needed to create them.
A script issues API calls in a specific order to build resources from an empty account.
Build the environment once from a golden image, then apply one-off manual fixes directly to the running servers as issues come up, without rebuilding the image.

rationale: Committing the file to version control and reusing it for every change is the IaC half of the proof; stating the desired end result rather than an ordered procedure is the declarative half. A documented runbook is still a set of ordered manual steps, not a file the tool itself reads and reapplies. An ordered API-call script may be versioned but lists steps rather than an end state, so it is imperative, not declarative. Patching a golden image's running servers by hand means the image no longer matches what is actually deployed, so nothing is left that is both current and declarative.
